title: Augmented integral reductions and fixed-interval completeness descent for a clopen cover
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$, $i\in I$, be a finite pairwise disjoint open and closed cover [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ and $R_i=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X_i}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and write $r_i$ for ordinary restriction on module sheaves, complexes and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $K\in D(R)$ and choose a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to K$ with $P$ K-flat and with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. In the reduction tower [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] set $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_{E,n})_X$, read as an $R$-complex by the quotient projection, $\gamma_n(p)=p\otimes1$, and $\tau_n(p\otimes a)=p\otimes\rho_n(a)$ for the coefficient reduction $\rho_n:A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$. Restriction sends $q$ to an admissible K-flat flat-term resolution and gives chain isomorphisms
$$r_iP_n\cong r_iP\otimes_{R_i}(A_{E,n})_{X_i},\qquad p\otimes a\longmapsto r_ip\otimes r_ia,$$
commuting with $\gamma_n$ and $\tau_n$. Consequently the derived reduction isomorphism $r_i(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})\cong (r_iK)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], also after restricting scalars, identifies the actual maps $c_n=[\gamma_n][q]^{-1}$ and $t_n=[\tau_n]$ with the component reduction maps. These comparisons are natural on derived objects and morphisms.

Writing $K_n=\operatorname{Res}_n(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$ and $c=(c_n)_n$, $K$ is derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete] if and only if every $r_iK$ is. More precisely, product and shift comparisons give a bijection between morphisms $\delta:\prod_nK_n\to K[1]$ and tuples $\delta_i:\prod_n(r_iK)_n\to(r_iK)[1]$; the triangle with arrows $c,1-s,\delta$ is distinguished exactly when each component triangle with its actual first map $(c_{i,n})_n$ is distinguished.

Membership in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and membership in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] are each equivalent to membership of every $r_iK$ in the corresponding category. For any fixed $a\le b$, all positive reductions of $K$ have cohomology supported in $[a,b]$ if and only if the same holds for every component and every positive reduction. The analogous equivalence holds for Tor amplitude in any fixed $[u,v]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. For nonempty $I$, component bounds $[a_i,b_i]$ and $[u_i,v_i]$ independent of $n$ give global bounds $[\min_i a_i,\max_i b_i]$ and $[\min_i u_i,\max_i v_i]$; any common larger bounds work as well. Empty components impose no conditions. For the empty partition $X=\varnothing$, all objects are zero, all conditions hold, and $[0,0]$ is an available uniform interval.

proof.text: Use the publicly re-exported ordinary finite restriction, exactness, augmented comparison and proved Roos descent from the compilation support module. These eight existing declarations keep their exact names, statements and data; the existing augmented comparison hole remains there unchanged.

Use the extracted, completely proved integral Roos calculation for the tuple derived equivalence, canonical countable-product comparisons and reflection of the actual limit triangles. The original private integralRoosCalculus signature is preserved by applying this result.

Apply [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] to $R$: its coefficient identifications preserve $\pi_n$, $\rho_n$ and $1$. By [lem-pur-finite-product-derived-tensor-calculus], restriction is exact, preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and preserves flatness and K-flatness. Thus $r_iq:r_iP\to r_iK$ is an admissible flat-term K-flat resolution. The same tensor comparison, with second factor $(A_{E,n})_X$ in degree zero, gives the asserted chain isomorphism $\beta_{i,n}:r_iP_n\to r_iP\otimes_{R_i}(A_{E,n})_{X_i}$ with the specified pure-tensor formula.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2, p. 24; agent finite-clopen application using the explicit reduction tower.

proof.text: The coefficient identifications give $\beta_{i,n}r_i\gamma_n(p)=r_ip\otimes1=\gamma_{i,n}(r_ip)$ and $\beta_{i,n}r_i\tau_n(p\otimes a)=r_ip\otimes\rho_{i,n}(r_ia)=\tau_{i,n}\beta_{i,n+1}(p\otimes a)$. These identities on local pure tensors determine the sheaf maps. Scalar restriction merely forgets part of the action, so preserves these equalities. Localize and compose the first identity with $[r_iq]^{-1}$: the maps $c_n$ and $t_n$ of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] become precisely $c_{i,n}$ and $t_{i,n}$. The derived scalar comparisons of [lem-pur-clopen-derived-scalar-compositor] are natural for all derived morphisms and have exactly these chain representatives. Independence of the augmented tower from $q$ is [lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined], which preserves both $c_n$ and $t_n$. Thus the calculation identifies the actual augmented towers, not only their level objects.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2, p. 24; agent finite-clopen application using the explicit reduction tower.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-clopen-strict-tower-roos-equivalence] to $C_n=P_n$ and $t_n=\tau_n$. It identifies products, their projections and $1-s$ with their component versions, and detects distinguishedness for the specified Roos triangle. By the fully faithful derived equivalence of [lem-pur-clopen-unbounded-derived-localization], a map $\delta:B\to K[1]$, $B=\prod_nK_n$, is equivalent to its tuple of component maps. Explicitly, if $\alpha_i:r_iB\cong B_i$ and $\sigma_i:r_i(K[1])\cong(r_iK)[1]$, the tuple is $\delta_i=\sigma_i r_i(\delta)\alpha_i^{-1}$. Conversely fullness gives a map from any such tuple, and faithfulness makes it unique. The product projections and Step 2 identify $r_i(c)$ with the actual component augmentation, so the distinguishedness assertion retains all three specified arrows.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2, p. 24; agent finite-clopen application using the explicit reduction tower.

proof.text: If $K$ is complete, choose its connecting map $\delta$ in [def-weil-derived-complete] and restrict the distinguished triangle using Step 3; each component is complete. Conversely choose a completing map $\delta_i$ for each complete component. The Hom bijection in Step 3 supplies $\delta$, and reflection of distinguishedness makes the triangle with first map $c$ distinguished. This proves both directions without selecting a canonical cone or claiming uniqueness of a completing map. In Lean the intrinsic completeness predicate is transported to the legacy predicate on slices by lem-sf-derived-complete-legacy-comparison; use the finite-field datum and the different-characteristic proof already supplied by the purity setting. No hypothesis on X is added.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2, p. 24; agent finite-clopen application using the explicit reduction tower.

proof.text: Apply lem-pur-integral-reduction-finite-clopen-bounds at each natural index n (positive exponent n+1). Its three assertions detect intrinsic torsion constructibility, support in a prescribed ordered interval, and Tor amplitude in a prescribed ordered interval for the actual reductions of the ordinary completed restrictions. Quantify over all n while keeping the interval fixed. The finite-level theorem itself uses the one-quotient comparison with the published ordinary constant-ring inverse image, not a parent integral-membership theorem.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1(1) and Definition 3.5.2, p. 24. Agent finite-clopen augmented reduction and uniform-bound application, returned proof steps 5-7.

proof.text: Assume $I$ is nonempty. Choose component cohomological intervals $[a_i,b_i]$ independent of $n$ and put $a=\min_i a_i$, $b=\max_i b_i$. Each component support lies in $[a,b]$, hence so does every global reduction by Step 5. Combine this with Step 4 and the constructibility part of Step 5 to obtain global membership in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Restricting proves the converse with the original global interval. For [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], repeat the same finite minimum/maximum construction with $[u_i,v_i]$ and the Tor assertion of Step 5, retaining the already proved constructible completeness conditions. This proves both integral membership equivalences and the claimed uniform bounds. Enlarging an interval preserves containment of supports and vanishing outside it.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2, p. 24; agent finite-clopen application using the explicit reduction tower.

proof.text: An empty component has zero module, complex and derived categories by [lem-pur-clopen-unbounded-derived-localization], so its reduction objects and all arrows vanish and it imposes no condition. If $I=\varnothing$, that same node gives $X=\varnothing$ and zero derived categories: there is one connecting map, its triangle is the zero distinguished triangle, and every reduction is zero. By [lem-pur-clopen-finite-constructibility-bounds], zero satisfies every fixed cohomological and Tor interval, in particular $[0,0]$. Thus the completeness and membership definitions used above hold also for the empty partition, with no minimum over an empty set.

proof_origin.place: The existing exactness, normalized Roos descent and augmented comparison plan are retained. Membership is assembled from the Roos Hom-bijection, the intrinsic/legacy completeness comparison, one positive quotient at a time, and finite minima/maxima. The one-quotient comparison is the only new unproved step; the strengthened augmented comparison remains open. X6 extracts the existing complete private integral Roos helper into a proved support module and preserves its private signature by a wrapper, solely for the per-file compile limit. After the private-helper split still left this file above 60 seconds, X6 extracts the existing prefix into AugmentedIntegralDescentCore and keeps the membership declaration and its proof unchanged in this facade. All original public imports remain.

Steps 1-2: the gluing node preserves pi_n, rho_n and 1 for the completed and finite coefficients. The finite-product node gives componentwise detection of flatness and K-flatness and the pure-tensor chain isomorphism. The compositor node localizes the same chain map. lem-weil-integral-reduction-tower-well-defined is in the route through the unit's use of sk-def-sf-operations. So the actual c_n and t_n are identified. Steps 3-4: the strict-tower Roos node keeps the first and connecting maps. The Hom bijection delta <-> (sigma_i r_i(delta) alpha_i^-1) comes from the fully faithful triangulated equivalence. Completeness follows in both directions from the existential definition, with c fixed and no canonical cone claimed. Steps 5-6: the bounds node is applied at each A_{E,n} with fixed intervals. Min/max over a finite nonempty I meets def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed (one support interval) and def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude (one Tor interval); l is invertible on X. Step 7: I covered empty components and I empty through the zero-category clauses, with [0,0] as the interval.
